record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: approximability of minimizing b for supermatches
record.original_question: For a given Stable Roommates instance, what approximation guarantees are achievable for finding a (1,b)-supermatch that minimizes the repair parameter b?

evidence.quote: Genc et al. [41] also provided two metaheuristics for finding a (1, b)-supermatch for a given sri instance that minimises the value of b, however, the approximability of this problem has not been studied theoretically.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an instance of the Stable Roommates problem (SR) consist of a set of an even number of agents, where each agent ranks all other agents in a strict order of preference. A matching M is a partition of the agents into pairs. A pair {x,y} not in M is a blocking pair of M if x prefers y to its partner in M and y prefers x to its partner in M; M is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Given a stable matching M and an integer b ≥ 0, M is called a (1,b)-supermatch if, for every pair {x, M(x)} in M, after removing that pair from M, the remaining matching on the other agents can be extended to a stable matching M' of the whole instance such that M and M' differ on at most b+1 pairs (equivalently, repairing the broken pair forces at most b further changes).

Problem: For a given SR instance, determine the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio achievable for the optimization problem of finding a (1,b)-supermatch that minimizes b. In particular, establish either approximation algorithms with provable performance guarantees, or inapproximability lower bounds (e.g., under P ≠ NP or standard complexity assumptions), for this minimization problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing work provides metaheuristics (local search and genetic local search) and a polynomial-time verification procedure for (1,b)-supermatches in the Stable Roommates problem, but no theoretical approximability results for minimizing b appear in the literature. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: An Approach to Robustness in the Stable Roommates Problem and its Comparison with the Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Local search and genetic local search procedures to find the (1,b)-supermatch minimising b in SR instances; verification via reduced rotation poset.
status_evidence.claim: Only heuristic/metaheuristic approaches are known; no approximation guarantees are established.

status_evidence.title: Stable roommates problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of stable roommates including robustness notions.
status_evidence.claim: No mention of approximation results for minimizing b in (1,b)-supermatches.
